rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the main uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model provides a useful baseline before testing more complex profile, aggregation, or fusion choices. config_001 tests the minimal RNA-only PCA single-profile setting, giving a reference for validation accuracy and F1. It is the best first experiment because it is simple, low-risk, and will help calibrate later comparisons to multiprofile aggregation, stronger RNA encoders, image-only models, and multimodal fusion without confounding multiple design changes at once.

The only completed experiment is an RNA-only PCA singleprofile baseline, so it is still unclear whether image features alone provide useful signal or whether multimodal fusion is worth pursuing. config_010 tests an image-only ResNet50 singleprofile model, the simplest image-modality baseline and the same image encoder used in many multimodal candidates. This is the best next experiment because it establishes a unimodal image reference without introducing fusion or multiprofile aggregation, enabling later comparisons to isolate the effect of adding RNA or fusion.

Existing evidence is sparse: RNA single-profile PCA is the best result so far (0.4849 accuracy, 0.4639 F1), while image-only ResNet is much weaker (0.2079 accuracy, 0.1718 F1). This supports exploiting the RNA direction before adding multimodal fusion. config_002 keeps the strongest known RNA encoder, pca_n2000, and tests whether moving from single-profile to multiprofile with simple avgpool aggregation improves performance. It is the best next experiment because it directly tests a central profile/aggregation design choice with minimal added complexity, avoids assuming that transformer aggregation or multimodality will help, and will clarify whether multiprofile RNA is worth pursuing before testing more complex configurations.

The strongest result so far is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002), which clearly outperforms single-profile RNA and image-only baselines. The main remaining uncertainty is whether transformer aggregation can improve on avgpool for the same multiprofile RNA representation. config_003 tests only this aggregation change, isolating its effect while exploiting the currently best design direction, making it a high-information and low-risk next experiment.

RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the strongest result so far (0.5907 accuracy, 0.5727 F1), clearly above single-profile PCA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is weak. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA representation can improve on PCA in this best profile/aggregation setting. config_005 keeps multiprofile avgpool and changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200, isolating the representation effect. This is the best next step because it exploits the strongest evidence, provides a clean comparison to config_002, may directly improve validation accuracy, and informs whether a learned RNA encoder should be used before adding multimodal complexity.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only models outperform image-only resnet50, that multiprofile avgpool improves PCA RNA from 0.485 to 0.591, and that scvi_n200 with multiprofile avgpool reaches the best result at 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1. The key uncertainty is whether scvi_n200 is intrinsically a better representation or whether its gain mainly comes from multiprofile aggregation. config_004 tests scvi_n200 in the singleprofile setting, changing only the RNA encoder relative to config_001. This cleanly isolates the representation effect, clarifies whether a simpler singleprofile scvi model can approach the best result, and avoids changing multiple design choices at once, making it a high-information next experiment under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile RNA with avgpool aggregation improves performance, and scvi_n200 is currently the best RNA encoder (config_005: 0.650 accuracy, 0.628 F1). However, scgpt is untested, so the key uncertainty is whether a different learned RNA representation can outperform scvi under the same favorable profile/aggregation setting. Testing config_008 isolates the effect of the RNA encoder by comparing scgpt to scvi and PCA while keeping multiprofile and avgpool fixed, making it a high-information next experiment before moving to more complex multimodal configurations.

The strongest evidence so far is RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation, which has the best validation accuracy and F1. Transformer aggregation was worse than avgpool for PCA, but it has not been tested with the stronger scvi representation. config_006 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer relative to the current best configuration, directly testing whether transformer aggregation can improve the top RNA-only model. This is a high-value next step because it exploits the most promising direction while isolating an important design choice, and it avoids prematurely testing more complex multimodal fusion before clarifying aggregation behavior.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only scvi_n200 with multiprofile aggregation is much better than PCA or scGPT, with config_006 and config_005 both around 0.65 validation accuracy and F1. Image-only resnet50 is weak, so the key uncertainty is whether adding image features to the best RNA setup can improve performance. config_032 keeps the best RNA encoder, profile setting, and aggregation fixed while adding resnet50 image features with simple concat fusion. This directly tests the marginal value of the image modality without confounding the result with an untested ViT-L encoder or weighted fusion, making it a focused exploitation of the strongest RNA evidence and a clean baseline for later fusion or image-encoder comparisons.

The strongest evidence is that scvi_n200 with multiprofile RNA is effective, and adding ResNet image features with transformer aggregation and concat fusion gives the best result so far (config_032, 0.688). However, image-only performance is weak, and RNA-only scvi shows almost no difference between avgpool and transformer aggregation, so it is unclear whether the transformer aggregation is actually necessary in the multimodal setting. config_030 changes only the aggregation from transformer to avgpool while keeping the best RNA encoder, image encoder, profile setting, and fusion method. This will clarify whether the multimodal gain depends on transformer aggregation or whether a simpler avgpool model is sufficient, while still exploiting the most promising configuration family.
